purpose: S4-18 curated localisation evaluation cases. Ground truth fixed BEFORE the localisation tool was run against it. Cases with no defensible ground truth were dropped, not guessed.
howEstablished: For every case the maintainer fix commit was read in full (GitHub commits API, application/vnd.github.diff) and the enclosing function of each changed non-test line was recorded by hand. The advisory text (GHSA and OSV records fetched 2026-09-06) was read to decide whether it names a function. The fixed release's registry gitHead was checked where npm publishes one.

conventions.expectedChangedFunctions: functions whose body the security fix changed; 'default' means the anonymous function assigned to module.exports
conventions.expectedPublicSymbols: the exported name an application would import or call, i.e. what Component 2 records as importedSymbol/calledSymbol
conventions.advisoryNamesFunction: true when the GHSA/OSV prose names a function or method

cases.notes: Baseline case: advisory names the function and the fix lands inside it. The diff hunk header is empty because every lodash function is indented inside an IIFE. 4.17.21 also fixes CVE-2020-28500 (toNumber/trim/trimEnd), so a version diff will show unrelated candidates.

The evaluation repository case (S4-20: Kirill89/prototype-pollution-explained calls _.merge on lodash 4.17.4). The fix changes only the private helper safeGet, which merge, mergeWith and defaultsDeep call through baseMergeDeep. A diff can name the helper; attributing it to the public API needs the advisory or a call graph. 4.17.4 to 4.17.11 spans seven releases.

fixCommits.source: GHSA references pull request lodash/lodash#4336; single commit

cases.notes: The only advisory reference is a pull request URL, not a commit, so the patch_reference path must resolve PR to commits. Same private-helper pattern as c02.

Alias case. The advisory names ini.parse; the changed function is decode, exported as `exports.parse = exports.decode = decode`. A diff-only method reports decode; joining to an application's ini.parse call needs export-alias resolution.

Multi-file, multi-function fix. The advisory names `new Range`; the diff touches the Range constructor, three Range methods, three module-level arrow helpers, the Comparator class and the regex table in internal/re.js. Measures how large a candidate set the diff methods produce when the fix is a refactor.

fixCommits.source: GHSA reference; 0.x line (v0.2.1), not applicable to 1.2.x

cases.notes: No function named. setKey is nested inside the anonymous default export (module.exports = function (args, opts)); the public symbol is the module itself. Two referenced commits belong to different release lines, so the tool must pick or report both.

No function named. One-line fix in lib/parse.js inside `var parseObject = function parseObjectRecursive(...)`, which has two names. The public entry is qs.parse in lib/index.js, a different file, so in-file alias resolution cannot bridge it.

cases.notes: No function named. Three referenced commits: one is the real 2.x fix, one is the 3.x fix, one changes no code at all. The npm tarball ships only the compiled lib/index.js bundle, so version_diff inspects generated code.

No function named. The whole package is one anonymous arrow function assigned to module.exports; the fix changes a regex string inside it. Tests the 'default' symbol convention and per-release-line commit selection.
No function named. Two private helpers change; the public symbol is the anonymous module.exports function that calls them via customDecodeURIComponent.

dropped.reason: Two fix commits across three release lines with different internal structure; no single defensible changed-function set without deeper reading than the budget allowed.
